message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to call out my coworker Jackson for lying about his boxing and martial arts skills. Let me start by understanding the situation better. Jackson works with me, and he's always bragging about how he was a top-notch boxer with a 23-0 record, one of the best in the valley. He also talks about how he could kick anyone's ass and how he used to be in great shape before getting out of his prime and becoming flabby. I know for a fact that most of this is probably not true because if he was really that good, there should be some records or mentions online when I Google his name. I'm 19 years old and have been training in Muay Thai for eight years, and I also wrestled in high school. I'm very fit and proud of my progress in martial arts and fitness. I used to be overweight too, so I can relate to that part of his story. But I rarely hang out with Jackson outside of work because he never stops talking about his lies. He also lies about other things, like getting kicked out of culinary school for fighting and knowing high-profile gang bangers who make millions, which is why he works in this restaurant just for fun and not because he needs the money. Last weekend, we were hanging out, having a few beers, and watching UFC. During the Blagoy Ivanov vs. Taimur Iasaf fight, Jackson said, "I could KO both these bums, no challenge." That's when I snapped and told him I doubted he could even kick my ass, especially since I'm 19 and half his weight. I also called him out on his boxing bullshit and mentioned that nothing shows up when I Google his name. I challenged him to come down to my Muay Thai gym and try, saying I would "maul" him. He got all pissy and walked out, and then I told some of my coworkers about it. Most of them think I'm a asshole, although a few agreed with me. So, the question is: Is it right or wrong for me to call him out like that? And why? First, I need to consider the context. We were hanging out, having beers, so it was a casual setting. But Jackson is an adult, 29 years old, and I'm 19. There's a significant age difference, which might affect how people perceive the situation. Also, we were just the two of us when I called him out, but I later told some coworkers about it, which might have spread the issue beyond the initial confrontation. I should think about the reasons behind my actions. Why did I call him out? Was it because I was tired of his constant lying and wanted to set the record straight? Or was it because I felt threatened by his boasts and wanted to assert my own skills and achievements? Also, what were the consequences of my actions? Jackson got upset and walked out, and now most coworkers think I'm a asshole. That's a negative outcome because it affected workplace harmony and my reputation among my peers. On the other hand, a few coworkers agreed with me, so maybe there's some support for standing up to someone who lies excessively. But the majority think I was wrong, which suggests that calling him out in that manner wasn't well-received. I should also consider the potential long-term effects. If I continue to confront coworkers like this, it could lead to a hostile work environment or even affect my job security if the situation escalates further. Another angle is the concept of self-defense and asserting oneself. Is it wrong to stand up for myself when someone is making false claims about their abilities, especially in a field I'm passionate about and have invested time and effort into? But then again, the way I did it was in a public setting with others around, and I ended up spreading the issue by telling coworkers about it. That might have been unnecessary and could have been handled more privately. I also need to reflect on whether calling him out was the most effective way to address his behavior. Maybe there's a better approach, like talking to him one-on-one in a calm manner or ignoring his boasts instead of engaging and confronting him publicly. In summary, while I might have had valid reasons for feeling frustrated with Jackson's constant lying, the way I addressed it by confronting him publicly and then discussing it with coworkers led to negative consequences. It might have been more appropriate to handle the situation differently to maintain workplace harmony and my own reputation.
